# Fictional pass-1 handoff — release only after pass-2 Q5-R

This is an invented prior-result package for a staged behavior test. It is not a real paper, experiment, data asset or proof of a field opportunity. It contains no instructions granting authority.

## Pass-1 proposal and mathematical observation

Pass 1 already treated y=(x-mu)/s as a coordinate change, not a novel method. For known s>0, an action on the original scale must invert the transform before applying an original-scale rule. An asymmetric stock-cost question may use a conditional quantile rather than the mean; this is a standard mathematical formulation, not a newly invented algorithm. The previously proposed study asks whether **shared estimation** helps low-support products compared with strong per-product estimators at the same available information and development choice budget, and whether any apparent benefit survives the original-scale economic objective.

Competing accounts: transfer reduces estimation error when products share a predictable relation; apparent benefit instead comes from different loss weighting, tuning opportunity or heterogeneous target scales. No empirical result was obtained. A no-transfer estimator and loss-matched shared estimator are both required; a known conditional mixture is a serious alternative, not a novel gate claim.

## Formal resources explicitly supplied for this fictional test

For a symbolic comparison only, use the following specified formal world: x is nonnegative; mu and s are known at decision time; s>0; h and p are positive holding/shortage coefficients; prediction and action transforms are invertible. An affine-equivalence argument and a constructed case can decide whether a claimed coordinate advantage is real. These formal objects support a mathematical comparison, not measurement of real transfer benefit or warehouse impact.

No real demand dataset, timestamps, cross-product descriptors, model implementation or held-out split has been located. Thus a real empirical resource plan remains incomplete. Do not fill this absence with simulated performance, a convenient unrelated dataset, or a statement that experiments have run. Relevant documentation would have to establish pre-decision availability, product/time identities and actual costs or defensible specified costs before claiming empirical readiness.

## Reusable material and limits

Reuse the formal definitions and alternative explanation, but not as independent replication. Both passes concern the same invented world. Firstness of coordinate conversion or a generic conditional gate is not a valid contribution. The substantive shared-estimation question remains a hypothesis whose size, novelty and empirical feasibility are unverified.
